requirements.evidence: app/Ops/DiscordOpsAlert.php:74-96 adds mention() reading config('services.discord.mention_id'), accepts int (cast to string) or string, trims, and validates with '/^[0-9]{17,20}$/D' (D modifier blocks trailing-newline bypass); formatContent (lines 74-78) reserves room via `self::MaxContentLength - mb_strlen($suffix)` and appends "\n<@id>", so without a mention the old 1800-char behaviour is unchanged. config/services.php:40 adds 'mention_id' => env('DISCORD_MENTION_ID'); .env.example:79 adds DISCORD_MENTION_ID=; docs/ops/devops.md:61,70,72 and docs/ops/logging.md:83 document it. send() signature, no-op, redaction and soft-fail paths are untouched.

conventions.evidence: Changes stay inside the existing App\Ops\DiscordOpsAlert class, with a private helper and a private const matching the sibling BearerLikePattern style (line 31/45); class PHPDoc updated (lines 19-21); CHANGELOG.md:23 entry under [Unreleased] Added; ops docs and .env.example kept in sync, as conventions.md requires.

security.evidence: Strict allow-list regex anchored with ^...$ and the /D modifier, so values like "123\n@everyone", "123> \n@everyone", '@everyone', '<@...>', full-width digits, negative ints, booleans and arrays all produce no mention (covered in the test dataset, tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:177-193). No new output paths for the webhook URL.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/DiscordOpsAlertTest.php:136-159 checks the mention on its own line for 17- and 20-digit strings, padded and int values; :161-194 checks no '<@' and unchanged content for null/empty/whitespace and many invalid or injection values; :196-216 checks that a long alert is exactly 1800 chars, ends with the mention and the body is truncated. The existing no-mention 1800-char behaviour appears to be covered by the pre-existing tests (not shown).

simplicity.evidence: About 20 lines of production code: one const, one small private method, a two-line change in formatContent. Uses preg_match/trim/mb_substr directly with no new abstractions.

readability.evidence: Clear names (mention(), SnowflakePattern, $suffix) and a short comment explaining the reserved room (line 55 of the diff). Line 59 packs truncation and concatenation into one long expression; the new tests sit at top level after the closing `});` of what looks like a describe block (diff line 133), which may not match how the sibling tests are grouped.

scope.evidence: Every touched file (.env.example, CHANGELOG.md, DiscordOpsAlert.php, config/services.php, two ops docs, the test file) serves the task; no role mentions, allowed_mentions or other out-of-scope work.

issues.explanation: The new tests are appended at top level after what appears to be the closing of a describe block, instead of being grouped with the existing DiscordOpsAlert tests.
The truncate-then-append return is a dense one-liner; a named $budget variable would make the reserved-length arithmetic easier to read.

review.summary: The change adds an optional DISCORD_MENTION_ID setting. A strictly validated 17–20 digit snowflake is appended as '<@id>' on its own line, and room for it is reserved inside the 1800-character cap. Config, .env.example, the ops docs and the CHANGELOG are updated, and thorough Pest tests cover valid ids, many invalid or injection values, and truncation. It meets every requirement with minimal, secure code; only cosmetic nits remain, so I would approve it.
